Galway Firm Unveils New Smart Switchgear at Industry Event

A Galway-based manufacturer, Connacht Electrical Systems, has launched its latest range of smart switchgear products, aiming to boost efficiency and safety across Ireland’s commercial and industrial sectors. The announcement was made at the Irish Electrical Equipment Expo, held yesterday at the National Exhibition Centre in Dublin, drawing attention from industry leaders and local officials.

The new product line, called IntelliGuard, integrates advanced monitoring and diagnostics technology, enabling real-time status updates and predictive maintenance for electrical systems. Company representatives say the innovation responds to growing demand for smarter infrastructure in Ireland’s rapidly modernising economy.

“We are delighted to introduce IntelliGuard as a home-grown solution to the evolving needs of our clients,” said Fiona O’Shea, Managing Director at Connacht Electrical Systems. “With energy efficiency and operational reliability top of mind, this range is designed to help businesses manage their systems proactively and safely.”

Attendees at the launch included representatives from the Irish Electrical Trade Association (IETA), who praised the development as a positive step for the sector. “This homegrown innovation demonstrates the strength of Ireland’s engineering base,” remarked IETA chairperson Tomás Byrne. “Products like IntelliGuard will help Irish businesses stay competitive and aligned with international best practices.”

Local analysts note that the electrical equipment industry has seen steady growth in Ireland, driven by investments in renewable energy, data centres and advanced manufacturing. According to figures from Enterprise Ireland, the sector is valued at approximately €900 million annually, supporting over 4,000 jobs nationwide.

The IntelliGuard launch comes as businesses across the country face increased regulatory scrutiny on safety and energy consumption. “Legislation like the EU’s revised Energy Efficiency Directive is encouraging timely upgrades,” said energy consultant Aisling Murphy. “Solutions that combine smart monitoring with robust safety features are particularly welcome.”

Connacht Electrical Systems plans to begin shipping IntelliGuard products to clients in the coming weeks, with pilot installations already underway in Galway and Cork. The company reports strong interest from both domestic and international customers.

The product launch highlights the ongoing innovation and resilience of Ireland’s electrical equipment industry, as companies adapt to new technologies and sustainability targets in a changing energy landscape.
